findings.title: Team admin/owner check requires both roles instead of either
findings.body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. A team admin who is not the owner, and in role models where admin and owner are distinct membership roles an owner who is not also recorded as admin, therefore fails the check. Despite the variable name and intended permission, the team admin/owner authorization path is effectively dead and those users receive FORBIDDEN unless they are also the organizer or an attendee. The condition should be an OR.

findings.title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials instead of the booking organizer's
findings.body: The handler explicitly permits non-organizers (team admins/owners and attendees), but then calls getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) and constructs EventManager from ctx.user. For those callers this does not contain the booking organizer's calendar credential/destination calendar, even though the booking query loaded booking.user with credentials. updateCalendarAttendees can therefore fail to update the organizer's external calendar, or attempt to use an unrelated credential of the caller, while the database attendees and emails claim the guests were added. The organizer's booking user/credentials should drive the calendar update.

findings.title: Guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, pending, or past bookings
findings.body: After loading the booking, the handler never checks booking.status or whether the event has ended before inserting attendees, updating the calendar, and sending emails. The new email templates generate ICS data with status CONFIRMED, so adding a guest to a cancelled booking can send a confirmed invitation and push attendees back toward the external calendar event, and adding guests to a past event sends meaningless invitations. The mutation, and ideally the UI action, should be restricted to appropriate upcoming confirmed bookings.

findings.title: Duplicate and blacklist checks are case-sensitive and do not deduplicate the request itself
findings.body: uniqueGuests filters only by exact `guest === attendee.email`, does not lowercase/trim guests, and does not deduplicate guests against each other; the server schema also only validates that each string is an email. Blacklisted addresses are lowercased before comparison while incoming guests are not, so `Blocked@Example.com` can bypass a lowercase blacklist entry. A direct tRPC caller can likewise submit the same address twice, or an existing attendee address with different casing, and create duplicate Attendee rows. Normalize emails and enforce uniqueness server-side before createMany.

findings.title: Email sender receives the raw guest list rather than the guests actually added
findings.body: The handler filters the request into uniqueGuests for insertion, but calls sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) with the original unfiltered list. In email-manager, any attendee whose email is in that list is classified as a new guest and receives AttendeeScheduledEmail. Consequently, when a request mixes an already-existing attendee with a genuinely new guest (reachable from the dialog, which does not know existing attendees), the existing attendee is sent a fresh full scheduling invitation even though they were not added. Pass uniqueGuests instead.

findings.title: Guest list has no maximum size
findings.body: guests is an unbounded array of emails. An authorized caller can submit thousands of addresses in one mutation, causing a large createMany, one translation load per attendee, a calendar update, and an email fan-out to every attendee. This enables resource exhaustion and use of the deployment as an invitation-email relay. Add a reasonable server-side max (and min) to the schema rather than relying on the dialog UI.

findings.title: Add-guests emails ignore disabled standard email settings
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails always sends organizer and attendee emails and does not accept or check eventTypeMetadata, unlike sendLocationChangeEmails and the other booking email helpers that honor disableStandardEmails for host/attendee. The handler loads booking.eventType but does not pass its metadata, so event types that have disabled standard emails will still generate these notifications. Thread the metadata through and apply the existing host/attendee disable checks.

findings.title: Invalid-email error state is not reset after success or dialog dismissal
findings.body: isInvalidEmail is set when validation fails, but the mutation onSuccess only resets multiEmailValue and closes the dialog; it does not reset isInvalidEmail. Closing via the dialog's onOpenChange (for example the X/Escape path) also bypasses the Cancel button's reset. Reopening Add Guests after a corrected, successful submission can therefore show 'Emails must be unique and valid' above a fresh empty form. Reset the flag on success and whenever the dialog closes or its value changes.
